text.p: Investors in the long term should hold shares of Polish industrial boilermaker Rafako SA, whose share price reflects the firm's market value, the brokerage unit of Bank Handlowy said in a report.

"We believe that the share price reflects the market value of the company, which is why we are issuing a long-term hold recommendation," Handlowy said in a report dated November 8 and released to the press on Monday.
On November 7 Rafako closed at 17.9 zlotys and fell to 14.4 zlotys on the Warsaw bourse on Friday. In that time the main market's index slipped to 13,531.1 from 13,919.8 points.

Handlowy said Rafako should be helped by demand from the outdated and inefficient domestic electrical power industry, which it said required immediate modernisation and could see $1-1.5 billion annual investment from 1997 to 2000.
It said planned privatisations in the sector could speed up the modernisation spending, which however could be delayed for political reasons before next year's parliamentary elections.
The report also said there was some uncertainty about total profits of the Rafako group as it had no uniform accounting standards for all subsidiary and associated firms.
Handlowy predicted Rafako would lift parent net profit to 12 million zlotys this year and 15.5 million zlotys next year from last year's 56.5-million-zloty loss.
It said sales would rise to 420 million zlotys this year and 530 million zlotys next year from last year's 359 million.
